newsitem.title: LEBANON: Solidere revenues, profits up in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Solidere revenues, profits up in 1996.

text.p: Lebanon's Solidere said on Monday its profits rose 81 percent in 1996 and revenues rose 70 percent due to strong land sales in the war-damaged Beirut Central District it is rebuilding.

Total revenues rose to $74.2 million from $43.5 million and net revenues from real estate activities were $43.7 million compared with $12.2 million in 1995, Solidere said in a statement reporting its unaudited results for 1996.
Net income was $58.5 million compared with the 1995 audited profit of $32.3 million.

The results showed that the company achieved its business plan objectives for the year and "exceeded its revenue projections as a result of strong land sales in the Beirut Central District," the statement said.
The balance sheet showed that Solidere's cash position at January 1, 1997, was $328.4 million.

Plans for 1997 included completing Solidere's first new landmark development in central Beirut -- a multi-storey headquarters for the U.N.'s Economic and Social Commission for Western Asia (ESCWA) to be delivered in September, the statement said.

Other major projects for 1997 included completing the restoration of nearly all buildings preserved in the city centre, launching a strong rental market in the district and starting key new development projects like building new souks, traditional housing and government developments.
